authorization.task: Keepraw Airport History — Owner Policy Change: Default Historical Continuity Since 2000
authorization.decision: For an airport code currently assigned to a known physical airport, assume that the same code-to-physical-airport assignment was continuously valid from 2000-01-01 unless affirmative evidence proves otherwise.
authorization.scope: This task authorizes the global passenger baseline, case-specific rebuttals from verified evidence, and the named Liuting and Jiaodong TAO intervals with both airport IDs preserved.

population.scheduled: All scheduled fixed-wing airports and seaplane bases in the pinned current snapshot.
population.regional: Other medium and large airports with a typed IATA code, plus small airports with both typed codes and a same-country BTS site match within 1 km.
population.selectionNote: BTS supports regional relevance and physical corroboration. Its USDOT codes supply neither IATA nor ICAO assignments.
population.evidenceExclusions: Outside the current-passenger denominator, retain the screened rows for documented former passenger sites, duplicate reference bindings and airports still under construction. Historical predecessor assignments remain in scope.

verification: Use the pinned typed IATA and ICAO fields independently and record the licensed physical-site reference.
Reuse existing airport IDs where the site matches. Confirm both identity and namespace before admitting an assignment.
Presume continuity from the cutoff for the ordinary current association and bind certain coverage only through the supported horizon.
Use affirmative evidence and explicit exceptions for former sites, code changes, dates after physical opening and metropolitan-only codes.
Keep conflicting current rows and materially unknown transitions unresolved. Directory revision timestamps supply no allocation dates.
Preserve old releases and authorization receipts. Current assignments cite this policy as continuity inference.
